chunks: From him, from al-‘Abbās, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Bakr ibn Sālim, from Sa‘d al-Iskāf, who said:
I heard Abā Ja‘far عليه السلام saying: “Whoever gives the adhān for seven years, seeking reward, will come on the Day of Resurrection having no sin.”

key_terms.أَذَّنَ: gave the adhān, meaning he performed the call to prayer
key_terms.احْتِسَابًا: seeking divine reward sincerely and with correct intention
key_terms.ذَنْبَ: sin or offense for which one is morally accountable
key_terms.سَبْعَ سِنِينَ: seven years, indicating sustained and continuous practice
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection, when people are raised for judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for giving the adhān for seven years with sincerity?
ai.summary: This hadith praises steadfast devotion in giving the adhān purely for the sake of Allah. It promises immense reward in the afterlife for one who performs this act of worship with sincere intention over a long period.
